pull.title: fix(stall): count buffered tool arguments as upstream progress
pull.body:
## What was wrong

A model that was **actively streaming a tool call** could be killed as a stall.

`req_e49840e712434d85ba85f0c4734b1e68` (`nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3`, streaming client, 66 tools) produced 1,333 chars of text and 3,625 chars of thinking, then died at `MODEL DEADLINE: stalled after 120s` with `tool_call_count` NULL — no tool call ever completed, and `ladder_tries=1`.

## Mechanism

The stall clock in `application/execution.py` resets `last_progress` only on a chunk for which `sse_carries_content()` is true — i.e. one containing a `content_block_delta`.

The openai_chat translator holds tool arguments back until the JSON parses:

- `Task` arguments accumulate in `ledger.blocks.buffer_task_args`;
- any tool whose argument names were **aliased for the wire** accumulates in `tool_argument_alias_buffers` until `_restore_aliased_tool_arguments` succeeds.

While buffering, `_emit_tool_arg_delta` yielded **nothing at all**. So the executor saw no content and measured the buffer instead of the model: a stream delivering a fragment every 100 ms was judged silent.

## Fix

The two buffering paths now yield `REASONING_HEARTBEAT` — the existing *"I consumed an upstream delta and have nothing to forward yet"* signal, already used by the reasoning holdback in `providers/stream_recovery.py:234-237`. The openai_chat stream loop forwards it **directly rather than through `hold_event`**, so it can never enter the holdback and commit the route on nothing. In `execution.py` the heartbeat branch now resets `last_progress` in addition to setting `reasoning_since`.

No new setting, no `.env.example` change, no `_chunk_timeout` change.

## What is explicitly unchanged

Dead-stream detection and fallback semantics are untouched — a stream that stops sending anything upstream sends no heartbeat either, so it is still killed.

Guard tests (all green):

- `tests/application/test_execution.py::test_a_buffering_stream_that_goes_silent_is_still_stopped` (new — buffering earns time only while upstream delivers)
- `::test_a_stream_that_goes_quiet_after_producing_is_stopped` (the 5.41.0 behaviour)
- `::test_a_keepalive_does_not_count_as_progress` (liveness is still not progress)
- `::test_a_buffered_request_that_stalls_falls_back_instead` (pre-commit fallback path)
- `::test_a_model_that_sends_no_first_token_hands_over_to_the_fallback`, `::test_the_first_token_deadline_stops_applying_once_output_started`, `::test_a_silent_model_is_still_judged_by_the_first_token_deadline` (first-token path goes to the next model)
- `::test_failure_after_the_first_chunk_is_never_retried_on_a_fallback`, `::test_fallback_runs_when_primary_fails_before_the_first_chunk` (commit boundary)

Retry / key-rotation invariants from #216, #209, #214 — **none of `providers/runtime/rotating.py`, `providers/credential_rotation.py`, `core/credential_rotation.py`, `providers/rate_limit.py` is touched by this PR.** Pinned and green:

- key health changes only on 401/403 and 429 — `tests/providers/test_credential_rotation.py::test_auth_failures_still_lock_out_and_escalate`, `::test_a_429_benches_for_the_configured_window_without_a_ladder`, `::test_only_key_shaped_failures_charge_health`, `::test_upstream_and_transport_failures_never_charge_health`, `::test_request_shaped_failure_leaves_health_byte_identical`, `::test_duck_typed_400_also_leaves_health_untouched`, `::test_repeated_400s_never_dry_up_a_healthy_pool`, `::test_nothing_else_ever_charges_a_credential`
- rotation allow-list = auth / 429 / connection errors, everything else raises to the next **model** — `::test_classified_auth_failures_justify_rotation`, `::test_unrelated_failures_do_not_escalate_the_auth_lockout`
- `acquire()` receives `unavailable | attempted` — `::test_acquire_avoids_unavailable_credentials`, `::test_acquire_falls_back_when_every_credential_is_unavailable`, `::test_unavailable_credentials_are_still_skipped_when_benched`, `::test_acquire_returns_minus_one_when_all_keys_benched`
- `openai.APITimeoutError` excluded from the transport-rotate check — `::test_timeout_leaves_health_untouched_and_does_not_rotate`, `::test_repeated_timeouts_never_exhaust_a_three_key_pool`, `::test_a_timeout_reaches_the_executor_with_the_pool_intact`
- preemption / bench accounting — `tests/providers/test_rotation_preemption.py` (all green)

## Proof

Three new tests in `tests/application/test_execution.py` drive the **real** `OpenAIToolCallAssembler` (not a hand-rolled generator) through `ProviderExecutor` with `stall_timeout=0.3` and a fragment every `0.1 s`:

- `test_buffered_task_arguments_do_not_starve_the_stall_clock`
- `test_buffered_aliased_arguments_do_not_starve_the_stall_clock`
- `test_text_at_the_same_cadence_is_never_cut` (control — identical timing, nothing buffered)

With `src/` stashed (i.e. on `fork/main`), the first two fail with the incident's own message:

```
E   my_claude_code.core.failures.ExecutionFailure: Provider 'primary/provider-model' stopped producing output for 0.3s.
FAILED tests/application/test_execution.py::test_buffered_aliased_arguments_do_not_starve_the_stall_clock
FAILED tests/application/test_execution.py::test_buffered_task_arguments_do_not_starve_the_stall_clock
2 failed, 3 passed in 14.60s
```

With the fix: `77 passed`.

## Verification

Local, Windows 11, Python 3.14.0, `uv`:

```
uv run pytest tests/application tests/providers -q --tb=line
  -> 3424 passed in 76.20s

uv run pytest tests/runtime -q --tb=line
  -> 1 failed, 58 passed in 29.87s
     (pre-existing: test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache)

uv run pytest -q --tb=line
  -> 15 failed, 7727 passed, 38 skipped in 326.44s

uv run ruff format      -> 990 files left unchanged
uv run ruff check --fix -> Found 1 error (1 fixed, 0 remaining)
uv run ty check         -> All checks passed!
```

**Baseline note:** the 15 failures are the known pre-existing set on this machine and are unrelated to this change — 8 websearch tests that read the real `~/.fcc/.env` (`tests/websearch/test_registry.py` x5, `tests/websearch/test_settings_websearch.py` x1, `tests/api/test_web_server_tools.py` x2), 6 `test_install_ps1_*` PowerShell installer tests, and `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`.

## On the incident's own tool list

Read read-only from `request_attempts.wire_body` for `req_e49840…`: 66 tools were sent. **2 of them alias** their argument names for the wire, both via `_fcc_arg_type` (the alias for a parameter literally named `type`, the only name `_needs_nim_tool_parameter_alias` rewrites):

- `Grep`
- `mcp__plugin_chrome-devtools-mcp_chrome-devtools__navigate_page`

`Task` was **not** in that tool list (this client sends `Agent` instead). Note that `-A/-B/-C/-i/-n/-o` are *not* aliased — they pass through unchanged.

**UNVERIFIED:** which tool the model was calling. The stream never emitted a tool name before it was killed, so it is not possible to say from the record that this bug caused `req_e49840e7`; the buffering starvation is proven as a defect in its own right by the tests above.

## Residual risks

- A provider that emits heartbeats indefinitely while genuinely making no progress would now hold an attempt until the **total** budget rather than the stall limit. That requires the translator to keep consuming upstream fragments, which is upstream liveness by definition; `total_timeout` still bounds it.
- The heartbeat is the empty string and is shared with the reasoning holdback, so the two are indistinguishable at runtime. That is deliberate — every forwarder writes nothing for either, and giving them separate but equal constants would add a name without adding behaviour.
- A `Task` fragment arriving after the arguments already emitted also produces a heartbeat. It is still "upstream delivered a fragment", so the semantics hold.

## Known and deliberate (not in this PR)

Once content has been committed, a mid-stream stall still **ends** the request rather than following the fallback chain. Resuming a committed Anthropic SSE message on another model is separate work.

stall. req_e49840e7 (nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3, 66 tools) streamed
1,333 chars of text and 3,625 of thinking, then died at
"MODEL DEADLINE: stalled after 120s" with tool_call_count NULL -- no tool
call ever completed.

Mechanism: the stall clock (application/execution.py) resets only on a
chunk for which sse_carries_content() is true, i.e. one containing a
content_block_delta. The openai_chat translator holds tool arguments back
until their JSON parses: Task args accumulate in buffer_task_args, and any
tool whose argument names were aliased for the wire accumulates in
tool_argument_alias_buffers until _restore_aliased_tool_arguments
succeeds. While buffering, the translator yields nothing at all, so the
executor sees no content and measures the buffer instead of the model.

Fix: the two buffering paths now yield REASONING_HEARTBEAT -- the existing
"I consumed an upstream delta and have nothing to forward yet" signal,

Dead-stream detection is unchanged: a stream that stops sending anything
upstream sends no heartbeat either, so it is still killed. Keepalives are
still not progress, the first-token path, _chunk_timeout, the commit
boundary and fallback semantics are untouched, and no setting was added.

Verification (local, Windows, Python 3.14.0):
- uv run pytest tests/application tests/providers -q --tb=line
  -> 3424 passed in 76.20s
- uv run pytest tests/runtime -q --tb=line

- Proof, with src/ stashed (pre-fix): the two new tests fail with
